In Bae, the 7th Circuit Court further interpreted the holding of Halper. In Bae, the court... by the ex post facto clause of the U.S. Constitution... In Bae, the circuit court rejected the defendant's argument that since debarment served both remedial and punitive goals it must be characterized as punishment. Bae's argument evidently relied on the Halper court's use of the word "solely" in the discussion leading to its holding. The circuit court's interpretation was much more pragmatic: "A civil sanction that can fairly be said solely to serve remedial goals will not fail under ex post facto scrutiny simply because it is consistent with punitive goals as well." 44 F. 3d at 493.
